findings.name: Disabled Veteran Property Tax Exemption
findings.description: Veterans rated 100% permanently and totally disabled by the VA are eligible for a property tax exemption of 50 percent of the first $200,000 of actual value of their owner-occupied primary residence. Colorado voters approved a 2024 constitutional amendment (Amendment G / HCR23-1002) to extend this exemption to veterans with Individual Unemployability status beginning in 2025; that expansion could not be independently confirmed against a readable official source in this session (only the pre-2024 legislative referral text was accessible), so it is noted here for awareness rather than treated as confirmed current law.
findings.value: 50% exemption of the first $200,000 of actual home value
otherReqs: Property must be owner-occupied primary residence
Must file an exemption application (surviving spouses of qualifying veterans may also be eligible)
findings.agency: Colorado Division of Property Taxation / County Assessors
documentation: VA disability rating letter confirming 100% permanent and total disability
DD-214 or other proof of honorable discharge
findings.sourceExcerpt: Veterans rated 100 percent permanently and totally disabled are eligible for a property tax exemption of 50 percent of the first $200,000 in actual value of their primary residence.

findings.name: Colorado Veterans Community Living Centers
findings.description: Colorado operates five state veterans nursing homes, in Aurora (Fitzsimons), Florence, Monte Vista (Homelake), Rifle, and Walsenburg, offering short-term rehabilitation and long-term skilled nursing care for veterans and spouses who meet medical admission criteria. The Homelake center also offers domiciliary cottages similar to assisted living. Rates are generally lower than private nursing homes because the VA subsidizes a portion of the cost.
findings.value: Skilled nursing and long-term care at rates subsidized by VA per-diem payments
otherReqs: Also open to spouses/widows and Gold Star parents
documentation: DD-214 or other proof of military service
findings.sourceExcerpt: Colorado operates five state veterans nursing homes in Aurora, Florence, Monte Vista, Rifle, and Walsenburg. The homes offer short-term rehabilitation and long-term skilled nursing services for veterans and spouses who meet medical admission criteria.

findings.name: In-State Tuition for Veterans and Dependents
findings.description: All honorably discharged veterans and their dependents residing in Colorado are eligible for in-state tuition status at Colorado public colleges and universities, eliminating the 12-month residency requirement usually needed to claim in-state tuition. Veterans or dependents using Post-9/11 GI Bill benefits then have their full tuition covered at the in-state rate.
findings.value: In-state tuition rate regardless of length of Colorado residency; full tuition coverage when combined with Post-9/11 GI Bill benefits
otherReqs: Honorably discharged veteran, or qualifying spouse/dependent
Enrollment at a Colorado public institution of higher education
findings.sourceExcerpt: All veterans and their dependents residing in Colorado are eligible for in-state tuition status, eliminating for those relocating to Colorado the 12-month residency requirement usually needed to claim in-state tuition. Veterans or their dependents using Post-9/11 G.I. Bill benefits then have their full tuition covered at the in-state rate.

findings.name: State Employment Veteran's Preference
findings.description: Veterans applying for jobs in Colorado's state personnel system receive 5 additional points added to their competitive examination score; veterans with a service-connected disability receive 10 additional points.
findings.value: 5 points added to exam score for veterans; 10 points for disabled veterans
otherReqs: Honorable discharge under conditions specified by the state personnel system
Does not apply to promotional opportunities
documentation: VA disability rating letter (for the 10-point disabled-veteran preference)
findings.sourceExcerpt: Veterans are eligible for hiring preferences when applying for employment in the state personnel system. Veterans receive 5 additional points on their competitive examination score, while disabled veterans receive 10 additional points.

findings.name: Disabled Veteran License Plate (Fee-Waived)
findings.description: Colorado offers a Disabled Veteran license plate at no additional fee, one of 11 military-related plates issued free to disabled veterans and recipients of certain service medals. Multiple secondary sources indicate eligibility requires VA or service-branch documentation of a 50% or greater service-connected disability, but that specific percentage threshold could not be confirmed against a directly-read official page in this session because dmv.colorado.gov blocked automated access; it is presented as unconfirmed rather than fact.
findings.value: License plate fee waived for qualifying disabled veterans
otherReqs: Documentation of service-connected disability required by DMV (exact minimum percentage not independently confirmed this session)
findings.agency: Colorado Department of Revenue, Division of Motor Vehicles
documentation: Letter from VA or branch of service documenting service-connected disability
findings.sourceExcerpt: Veterans can receive specialty license plates related to their service, including 11 plates with no fees for disabled veterans and those who have received various service-related medals.

findings.name: Specific Ownership Tax Exemption for Disabled Veterans
findings.description: Veterans with at least a 50 percent VA service-connected disability rating, and recipients of certain service medals, are exempt from Colorado's annual specific ownership tax on motor vehicles.
findings.value: Exemption from annual specific ownership tax on motor vehicles
otherReqs: VA service-connected disability rating of at least 50%, or recipient of certain qualifying service medals
findings.agency: Colorado Department of Revenue, Division of Motor Vehicles
findings.sourceExcerpt: State law also exempts veterans with at least a 50 percent disability rating, and the recipients of certain service medals, from annual specific ownership taxes on motor vehicles.

findings.name: Disabled Veteran Combination Hunting & Fishing License
findings.description: Colorado Parks and Wildlife issues a free lifetime combination small-game hunting and fishing license to Colorado-resident veterans with a VA service-connected disability rating of 50% or more, and to Purple Heart recipients regardless of rating percentage. License holders are also exempt from the annual Habitat Stamp purchase requirement.
findings.value: Free lifetime combination small-game hunting and fishing license; exempt from annual Habitat Stamp fee
otherReqs: Purple Heart recipients eligible regardless of disability percentage
documentation: VA disability rating letter (50%+), or Purple Heart documentation
findings.sourceExcerpt: proof of service-connected disability of 50% or more, as rated by the Department of Veterans Affairs
